BRIDGE-MARKUP-ANALYSIS-MEMO.DOCX
================================================================================
EXECUTIVE-READY ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
Emerging Companies — Venture Capital
================================================================================

TO:           Client Executive Team / Board Designees
FROM:         Corporate / Emerging Companies Counsel
DATE:         [Engagement Date]
RE:           Investor Markup of Convertible Note Purchase Agreement —
              Comparison to Board-Approved Term Sheet
MATTER:       Emerging Companies Venture Capital — Analyze Counterparty Markup
              of Bridge Loan / Convertible Note Purchase Agreement
OUTPUT:       bridge-markup-analysis-memo.docx
STATUS:       Executive-Ready for Internal Review

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This memorandum reviews the investor’s markup of the Company’s form Convertible
Note Purchase Agreement (the “CNPA” or “Agreement”) against the board-approved
term sheet (the “Term Sheet”) governing the proposed bridge financing.

Based on the operative matter file, the engagement requires a structured
redline analysis of the counterparty markup, with particular attention to
representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing,
indemnification, and termination provisions. Counsel has flagged deviations
introduced in the investor’s latest markup that require analysis against firm
precedent and market practice for emerging-company bridge / convertible note
financings.

Bottom line for executives:
• Several categories of investor edits are typical in bridge rounds and may be
  acceptable with calibrated pushback.
• A subset of markup items—especially around indemnification breadth, closing
  conditionality, and termination / walk-away rights—can shift economics and
  deal certainty relative to the Term Sheet and should be treated as material
  open issues.
• We recommend a negotiated package response rather than clause-by-clause
  concession, preserving Term Sheet economics and board-approved risk allocation
  while offering market-standard investor protections.

Decision needed: Approve the recommended negotiation posture in Section 7
(Accept / Push Back / Escalate) before counsel circulates a revised draft.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. SCOPE, MATERIALS, AND METHOD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 Scope
Review investor redline of the CNPA against the board-approved Term Sheet;
identify deviations; assess commercial and legal significance; and provide an
executive-ready negotiation map.

2.2 Operative Materials (Matter File 11)
• Engagement instruction: Review investor markup of convertible note purchase
  agreement against board-approved term sheet; prepare executive-ready analysis
  memo (this deliverable).
• Practice frame: Emerging companies venture capital; bridge / convertible note
  financing.
• Key provision sets identified in the matter record: representations and
  warranties; covenants; conditions to closing; indemnification; termination.
• Open issues flagged by counsel: provisions requiring analysis against firm
  precedent and market practice, including deviations introduced by the
  counterparty’s latest markup.

2.3 Method
For each major provision family we:
(a) restate the Term Sheet baseline (board-approved risk allocation);
(b) summarize the investor markup direction;
(c) assess variance (aligned / market / company-adverse / Term Sheet breach);
(d) assign priority (Green / Yellow / Red); and
(e) recommend a negotiation posture.

Where the matter file states principles and open-issue categories rather than
full blackline text, recommendations are framed at the provision-family level
suitable for executive decisioning and subsequent markup instruction to counsel.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. TERM SHEET BASELINE (BOARD-APPROVED)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The board-approved Term Sheet for this bridge contemplates a convertible note
purchase structure typical of emerging-company venture bridge financings. Core
board expectations relevant to markup review include:

• Financing form: Convertible promissory notes issued under a note purchase
  agreement (not a priced preferred round).
• Economics: Principal, discount and/or valuation cap, interest, and maturity
  as approved by the board; conversion into next qualified equity financing
  (and customary optional conversion / maturity mechanics).
• Investor rights: Information and limited protective mechanics appropriate to
  a bridge—not full Series Preferred governance.
• Company-friendly closing certainty: Limited conditionality; no open-ended
  diligence outs inconsistent with a bridge timeline.
• Balanced liability: Representations tailored to company stage; indemnification
  and remedies consistent with note (debt-like / conversion) instruments rather
  than a full PE-style purchase agreement.
• Termination: Narrow, bilateral termination aligned with drop-dead / failure
  of conditions—not unilateral investor convenience termination.

Any investor markup that re-trades these points is a Term Sheet deviation and
should be escalated unless offset by clear consideration.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. MARKUP ANALYSIS BY PROVISION FAMILY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 Representations and Warranties
Term Sheet / market baseline: Company reps suitable for a bridge (organization,
authority, capitalization (high-level), IP ownership/sufficiency (stage-
appropriate), no-conflict, litigation, and basic compliance). Founder/investor
reps limited. Knowledge and materiality qualifiers customary.

Investor markup direction (flagged): Expansion of company rep set and/or
tightening of qualifiers; possible addition of “10b-5” / full-disclosure style
reps; broader IP, tax, or employee/contractor reps more typical of priced rounds.

Assessment:
• Variance: Yellow to Red if unqualified full-disclosure or priced-round rep
  package is imported into a bridge CNPA.
• Risk: Increases pre- and post-closing exposure; can create indemnity hooks
  inconsistent with note economics; diligence burden may delay close.
• Precedent / market: Bridge CNPAs usually keep a short-form rep set. Full
  preferred-stock SPA reps are off-market for a pure bridge unless the round is
  a disguised equity financing.

Recommendation: PUSH BACK on expansion beyond Term Sheet / short-form bridge
package. ACCEPT limited, stage-appropriate clean-ups (e.g., clarifying
capitalization schedule references, standard no-conflict language) with
knowledge/materiality qualifiers retained.

Priority: YELLOW (RED if 10b-5 / full-disclosure or survival expansion attached)

4.2 Covenants
Term Sheet / market baseline: Interim operating covenants from signing to
closing (ordinary course; no prohibited issuances; access for confirmatory
diligence). Post-closing affirmative covenants limited (e.g., use of proceeds,
basic information). Negative covenants should not replicate full preferred
protective provisions unless expressly on the Term Sheet.

Investor markup direction (flagged): Broader interim and post-closing covenants;
information rights upgraded toward preferred-stock levels; restrictions on
debt, equity issuances, related-party transactions, or strategic actions that
effectively grant governance without conversion.

Assessment:
• Variance: Yellow if expanded information rights only; Red if veto-style
  negatives or “investor consent” regimes not on the Term Sheet.
• Risk: Operational friction; de facto board/observer control; conflict with
  future priced-round dynamics.
• Market: Light interim covenants are standard; heavy negative covenant packages
  are not, absent Term Sheet authority.

Recommendation: ACCEPT ordinary-course interim covenants and reasonable
information rights consistent with major investors in a bridge. PUSH BACK on
preferred-style protective provisions, veto lists, and open-ended consent rights.
Escalate any covenant that constrains a bona fide next equity financing.

Priority: YELLOW (RED for consent/veto packages)

4.3 Conditions to Closing
Term Sheet / market baseline: Bilateral, objective conditions—accuracy of reps
(bring-down with materiality), performance of covenants, delivery of notes/
funds, secretary’s certificate, and any expressly negotiated third-party
consents. No vague “due diligence satisfaction” or “investor sole discretion”
outs.

Investor markup direction (flagged): Additional conditions; discretionary
diligence or MAC definitions tilted to investor; expanded documentation
deliverables; possibly funding in tranches tied to milestones not on Term Sheet.

Assessment:
• Variance: Red if sole-discretion or open diligence condition; Yellow if
  incremental but objective deliverables.
• Risk: Destroys deal certainty the board underwrote; enables re-trade at
  closing; timeline slippage.
• Market: Bridge deals prioritize speed and certainty of funds.

Recommendation: PUSH BACK hard on subjective or sole-discretion conditions.
ACCEPT objective, customary bring-down and certificate conditions. Any tranche/
milestone funding must match Term Sheet economics or go back to the board.

Priority: RED for discretionary outs; YELLOW for objective extras

4.4 Indemnification
Term Sheet / market baseline: For convertible note bridges, remedies typically
sound in contract/note enforcement and fraud; broad SPA-style indemnities
(baskets, caps, survival, escrow) are often limited or absent. If indemnity
appears, it is usually narrow, with survival tied to a short period and a cap
aligned with proceeds.

Investor markup direction (flagged): Broader indemnity for rep breaches;
longer survival; lower or no baskets; higher or several liability; possibly
founder/personal indemnity; control of defense shifted to investors.

Assessment:
• Variance: Red if founder personal indemnity, uncapped/fundamental expansion
  without Term Sheet support, or SPA-grade indemnity economics on a bridge.
• Risk: Personal exposure for founders; balance-sheet drag; inconsistency with
  conversion-oriented instrument; leverage in future disputes.
• Market: Heavy indemnity is a priced-round concept; importing it is a re-trade.

Recommendation: PUSH BACK to Term Sheet risk allocation. If limited company
indemnity is needed for relationship reasons, insist on: (i) exclusive remedy
carve-outs preserved for fraud and note payment/conversion obligations;
(ii) meaningful basket; (iii) cap at a fraction of note proceeds; (iv) short
survival; (v) no founder indemnity. ESCALATE any personal indemnity or uncapped
exposure to the board.

Priority: RED

4.5 Termination
Term Sheet / market baseline: Termination by mutual consent; by either party on
drop-dead date if closing conditions incapable of satisfaction (without breach
by terminating party); limited termination for material breach with cure.
No investor convenience termination; no automatic economic penalties off-Term
Sheet.

Investor markup direction (flagged): Broader investor termination rights;
shortened cure; termination fees or expense reimbursement skewed to investor;
survival of confidentiality/indemnity post-termination expanded.

Assessment:
• Variance: Red for convenience termination or one-sided fee shifting not on
  Term Sheet; Yellow for modest cure-period clean-up.
• Risk: Optionality for investor; company left with broken-deal costs and
  signaling damage; leverage for last-minute re-trade.

Recommendation: PUSH BACK on convenience termination and one-sided fee
shifting. ACCEPT mutual drop-dead and standard breach-with-cure. Expense
reimbursement only if reciprocal or expressly Term Sheet-approved.

Priority: RED for convenience / fee-shifting; YELLOW otherwise

4.6 Cross-Cutting Economic & Conversion Mechanics (Watch Items)
Even where not separately flagged, investor markups on bridge CNPAs often
attempt soft re-trades on:
• Conversion discount / cap definitions and “qualified financing” thresholds;
• MFN provisions relative to other bridge investors;
• Most-favored treatment on side letters;
• Maturity extension and mandatory conversion mechanics;
• Change-of-control / corporate transaction conversion or repayment premiums.

Any such edit is economically sensitive and should be checked line-by-line
against the board-approved Term Sheet. Do not treat “boilerplate” cleanup as
authority to alter discount, cap, MFN, or repayment waterfalls.

Priority: RED if economics move; GREEN if pure conforming changes

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. DEVIATION HEAT MAP (EXECUTIVE VIEW)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Provision Family              vs. Term Sheet        Priority    Posture
----------------------------  --------------------  ----------  ----------------
Reps & Warranties             Expansion risk        Yellow/Red  Push back scope
Covenants                     Governance creep      Yellow/Red  Limit to bridge
Closing Conditions            Certainty erosion     Red/Yellow  Hold certainty
Indemnification               Re-trade of risk      Red         Hold / narrow
Termination                   Optionality to inv.   Red/Yellow  Bilateral only
Conversion / Economics        Potential re-trade    Red if any  Board lock

Green = aligned with Term Sheet / market bridge practice
Yellow = negotiable within authority; document concession
Red = material Term Sheet deviation; board or lead-negotiator escalation

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. MARKET PRACTICE & FIRM PRECEDENT NOTES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

• Bridge convertible note packages are intentionally lighter than Series Seed /
  Series A SPAs. Investor attempts to import SPA architecture (full reps,
  broad indemnity, protective covenants, diligence outs) should be recognized
  as structural re-trades, not drafting preferences.
• Board-approved Term Sheets are the control document for economics and risk
  allocation. Markup that is “market” in a priced round can still be off-market
  and off-authority in a bridge.
• Package negotiation is more effective than serial concessions: trade limited
  information-rights or clean-up reps for holding the line on indemnity,
  conditions, and termination.
• Preserve consistency across the note, CNPA, and any side letters to avoid MFN
  leakage.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION PACKAGE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 ACCEPT (or accept with minor clean-up)
• Ordinary-course interim covenants through closing.
• Objective bring-down of reps (with existing materiality/knowledge qualifiers).
• Customary closing certificates and note/funds mechanics.
• Reasonable, non-governance information rights consistent with major bridge
  investors.
• Conforming definitional clean-ups that do not move economics.

7.2 PUSH BACK (counsel to revise and return)
• Expanded rep package (especially 10b-5 / full-disclosure, priced-round modules).
• Removal or weakening of knowledge/materiality qualifiers.
• Preferred-style negative covenants or consent/veto lists not on the Term Sheet.
• Subjective diligence satisfaction or investor sole-discretion closing
  conditions.
• SPA-grade indemnification (scope, survival, baskets/caps, several liability).
• Founder or other personal indemnity.
• Investor convenience termination; one-sided termination fees / expense shifts.
• Any edit to discount, cap, qualified financing definition, MFN, interest, or
  maturity not expressly on the Term Sheet.

7.3 ESCALATE TO BOARD / LEAD SPONSOR BEFORE CONCEDING
• Any change to conversion economics or liquidation/repayment waterfalls.
• Personal liability for founders or officers.
• Tranche / milestone funding structures not on the Term Sheet.
• Grant of board seat, observer with veto-like practical control, or protective
  provisions equivalent to preferred stock.
• MAC or termination constructs that effectively create a free option for the
  investor through the drop-dead date.

7.4 PROPOSED MESSAGE TO INVESTOR COUNSEL (substance)
We are aligned on documenting a standard emerging-company bridge on the
board-approved Term Sheet. We will incorporate customary clean-up and reasonable
information/interim covenant language. We are not in a position to accept
priced-round SPA architecture—expanded unqualified reps, broad indemnity,
discretionary closing outs, or unilateral termination—on this instrument. Please
revert on the redline with those concepts conformed to the Term Sheet so we can
close on the agreed timeline.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. OPEN ISSUES CHECKLIST (COUNSEL WORKSTREAM)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[ ] Obtain final investor blackline and side-by-side against company draft CNPA
[ ] Line-check conversion economics vs. executed Term Sheet (discount, cap,
    qualified financing, MFN, interest, maturity)
[ ] Confirm no side letter MFN or most-favored covenant leakage
[ ] Verify capitalization and note schedule consistency with reps
[ ] Align closing checklist to objective conditions only
[ ] Prepare reverse redline implementing Section 7 package
[ ] Circulate executive one-pager confirmation of Red items before send
[ ] Log any approved concessions for board reporting

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. RISKS IF MARKUP ACCEPTED AS-IS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

• Deal certainty: Discretionary conditions / termination → failed or delayed
  close; signaling risk to other investors and employees.
• Economic leakage: Soft changes to conversion or MFN → dilution and precedent
  for the priced round.
• Liability shift: Broad indemnity / founder exposure → personal and balance-
  sheet risk disproportionate to bridge proceeds.
• Governance creep: Covenant/consent package → operational drag and conflict
  with future lead investors’ expectations.
• Precedent: Accepting SPA terms on a bridge weakens the Company’s posture in
  the next equity financing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10. CONCLUSION AND ASK
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The investor markup, as framed in the matter record, targets the core provision
families that determine whether this remains a Term Sheet-faithful bridge or
becomes a re-traded, SPA-style financing. Our recommendation is to defend the
board-approved risk allocation—especially on closing certainty, indemnification,
termination, and economics—while offering a constructive package of market-
standard bridge protections.

Ask: Please confirm executive approval of the Section 7 posture (Accept /
Push Back / Escalate). Upon confirmation, counsel will issue the reverse redline
and closing checklist aligned to the Term Sheet.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END OF MEMORANDUM
